questions.q: What activated the flight termination system of the Matternet M2 in Zurich?
options: Loss of link with the operator's radio
questions.explain: Vibration on IMU3 → EKF divergence → FTS.

questions.q: Why didn't the parachute save the Matternet M2?
options: It was too small for that mass
questions.explain: The line didn't survive the jerk because of prior damage.

questions.q: What did the Airspeeder's controller do on link loss?
options: Engaged RTH to the takeoff point
questions.explain: It froze the throttle and held level — the aircraft climbed to ~7900 ft. A “hold” failsafe instead of “descend” is the main lesson.

questions.q: Why was the cause of the Airspeeder's link loss not determined?
options: The board didn't look for the cause
questions.explain: Without a log an investigation ends with the words “not determined”.

questions.q: What caused the Alta X to crash?
options: Battery depletion because of the threshold
questions.explain: The warning threshold was lowered from 44 to 42 V and the voltage wasn't checked before takeoff: there was no hardware failure.

questions.q: What impact energy is taken as the threshold for a risk of serious injury?
questions.explain: The Matternet without payload is already 118 J.

questions.q: The common conclusion of the three cases:
questions.explain: What the aircraft does when something goes wrong is the engineer's main question.

questions.q: Why does a crash analysis look for the root cause in the process rather than in the person?
options: The process can be changed so the error doesn't repeat with anyone
So that nobody is held responsible for the crash
questions.explain: Changing the process protects against a repeat regardless of who does the work.
